title: 1998 AHSME Problem 19
statement: How many triangles have area \(10\) and vertices at \((-5,0),\) \((5,0),\) and \((5\cos\theta,5\sin\theta)\) for some angle \(\theta?\)

solutions.text: The area is \(\frac12(10)|5\sin\theta|=25|\sin\theta|.\) Thus \(|\sin\theta|=\frac{2}{5}.\) There are four corresponding points on the circle, and each gives a distinct triangle. Hence the answer is \(4,\) making C correct.
hints: The fixed base has length \(10\), and the third vertex has height \(|5\sin\theta|\)
Count the distinct points on the circle satisfying the resulting sine equation
